1	# Claude Code Background Sessions Scope
2	
3	## 1. Problem
4	
5	The Control Room already hosts a native supervisor surface for OpenCode:
6	`admin/opencode_client.py` talks to the running OpenCode server, and
7	`scripts/supervise.py` relays native sessions into the Control Room's
8	Redis-backed event streams and flags stalled/off-track work for human review.
9	There is no equivalent surface for Claude Code's own background-session
10	mechanism.
11	
12	`src/instrument/claude_adapter.py` drives the `claude` CLI today, but only in
13	headless, single-shot mode: `run_claude_agentic` builds one
14	`claude -p "<prompt>" --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions
15	[--model ...]` subprocess, streams its `stream-json` events through
16	`ClaudeStreamAdapter`, and returns when that one process exits
17	[src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:236-346]. It never enumerates, attaches to,
18	or controls a `claude --bg` background session, and it maps the framework's
19	advisor-model id `claude-fable-5` to `claude-sonnet-5` for the primary model
20	[src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:185-211] — Claude Code's own
21	`--advisor fable` server-side advisor is a distinct mechanism, unused today.
22	
23	Claude Code separately ships a background-session product: `claude --bg`
24	starts a supervised session that keeps running after the launching terminal
25	exits, `claude agents` lists and monitors those sessions, and `claude attach`,
26	`claude logs`, `claude stop`/`kill`, `claude respawn`, and `claude rm` manage
27	one session's lifecycle, all hosted by a `claude daemon` supervisor process.
28	None of this is visible from the Control Room. An operator who dispatches a
29	`claude --bg` task today has no fleet card, no transcript, and no lifecycle
30	controls inside the command rail — they have to shell out separately, which
31	is exactly the gap the OpenCode native surface already closed for OpenCode.
32	
33	This feature adds the Claude analog: list, observe, and lifecycle-control
34	`claude --bg` sessions and the `claude daemon` that hosts them, inside the
35	existing Control Room, reusing its command-rail aesthetic and SSE/Redis
36	transport rather than building a second dashboard.
37	
38	## 2. Investigated CLI Facts
39	
40	Investigated against the Claude Code CLI reference,
41	<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference>. Commands and flags below are
42	quoted from that reference; anything not stated there is called out as not
43	possible rather than inferred.
44	
45	### Starting a background session
46	
47	- `claude --bg "<task>"` / `claude --background "<task>"` — starts the task as
48	  a background agent and returns immediately, printing the session ID and
49	  management commands. Cannot be combined with `-p`/`--print`. Can combine
50	  with `--exec` to run a shell command as a background job instead of a Claude
51	  session, and with `--agent` to run a specific subagent.
52	- `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, when set on a `--bg` launch, persists
53	  across supervisor restarts for that session (i.e., a respawn keeps the
54	  original permission mode).
55	
56	### Listing / observing
57	
58	- `claude agents` — opens an interactive terminal "agent view" for monitoring
59	  and dispatching background sessions; **requires an interactive terminal**,
60	  so it is not something a Flask backend can drive headlessly.
61	- `claude agents --json` — prints active sessions as a JSON array, scriptable.
62	- `claude agents --json --all` — same, but includes completed background
63	  sessions.
64	- `claude agents --cwd <path>` — restricts the listing to sessions started
65	  under that directory.
66	- `claude logs <id>` — prints recent output from one background session. This
67	  is a plain, non-interactive stdout dump — safe to call headlessly and diff.
68	- `claude attach <id>` — attaches to a background session **in a terminal**
69	  to view and follow it live; the reference explicitly scopes this to
70	  "view/follow," not steering input, and — like `claude agents` — implies a
71	  real interactive TTY, not a scriptable stream.
72	- `claude daemon status` — prints the background-session supervisor's state,
73	  version, socket directory, and worker count; exits 1 if the supervisor
74	  isn't running.
75	
76	### Lifecycle control
77	
78	- `claude stop <id>` / `claude kill <id>` (`kill` is an alias for `stop`) —
79	  stops a background session.
80	- `claude respawn <id>` — restarts a background session, running or stopped,
81	  **with its conversation intact**. `claude respawn --all` restarts every
82	  running session (e.g., to pick up an updated Claude Code binary).
83	- `claude rm <id>` — removes a session from the list. The transcript is not
84	  deleted; it stays on disk and remains reachable via `claude --resume`.
85	- `claude daemon stop --any` — stops the background-session supervisor and
86	  every session it hosts. `--any` is required to confirm stopping an
87	  on-demand supervisor (the default supervisor kind). `--keep-workers` leaves
88	  the background sessions running so the next supervisor reconnects to them
89	  instead of killing them. This is the documented recovery path for an
90	  unresponsive supervisor.
91	
92	### Advisor
93	
94	- `--advisor <model>` (e.g. `--advisor fable`, `--advisor opus`,
95	  `--advisor sonnet`, or a full model ID) enables the server-side advisor tool
96	  for a session, and works with any session mode, including background
97	  (`claude --bg --advisor fable "task"`). `fable` requires Fable 5 access. It
98	  takes precedence over the `advisorModel` setting. This is a pass-through
99	  launch flag, not something the Control Room implements — it only needs to
100	  be exposed as an optional start-time input.
101	
102	### What is explicitly NOT possible
103	
104	The reference documents no way to send input to, or otherwise interactively
105	steer, a *running* background session. `attach` is view/follow only; there is
106	no `claude bg send`, no prompt-injection command, and no documented
107	`delivery: steer` equivalent to OpenCode's native
108	`POST /api/session/{id}/prompt` [contrast with admin/opencode_client.py:94-102].
109	Concretely:
110	
111	- **Interrupt has no direct analog.** OpenCode's `interrupt` stops active work
112	  *without* ending the session [admin/opencode_client.py:104-107]. Claude
113	  Code's closest primitives are `stop` (ends the session; conversation is
114	  preserved but the process is gone) and `respawn` (restarts the session with
115	  its conversation intact, effectively resuming after a stop). Neither is a
116	  live, in-flight interrupt-and-keep-running.
117	- **There is no send-input / steer control.** This spec deliberately does not
118	  invent one. Any control surface for background sessions is limited to the
119	  lifecycle verbs the CLI actually exposes: stop/kill, respawn, rm, and
120	  daemon stop.
121	- **`claude agents` and `claude attach` need a real TTY**, so this feature
122	  uses only the scriptable subset (`claude agents --json --all`,
123	  `claude logs <id>`, `claude daemon status`, and the lifecycle commands)
124	  driven via `subprocess`, the same way `claude_adapter.py` already drives the
125	  CLI for headless runs [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:291-299].
126	
127	## 3. Chosen Integration Approach
128	
129	### Decision
130	
131	Add a small `admin/claude_agents_client.py` subprocess wrapper around the
132	scriptable `claude` subcommands above (list, start, logs, stop, respawn, rm,
133	daemon status), mirroring the shape of `OpenCodeClient`
134	[admin/opencode_client.py] but calling a CLI instead of an HTTP API. Add a
135	lightweight poller (module-level thread or endpoint-triggered refresh, not a
136	new always-on service) that periodically runs `claude agents --json --all` to
137	refresh a Redis-cached roster, and — for the currently selected/attached
138	session only — diffs `claude logs <id>` output and republishes new lines
139	through the existing `LivePublisher` event/log channel used by
140	`instrument/live.py`, under a distinct `cell_id` namespace (e.g.
141	`claude_bg_<session-id>`). The existing `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` SSE
142	endpoint, its retained-history replay, and its `replay_complete` boundary
143	[admin/server.py:450-490] then serve the transcript with zero new SSE
144	machinery. Add new `POST`-mutating endpoints for start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon
145	actions, all behind the loopback + JSON + Idempotency-Key guard the
146	design-session endpoints already enforce [admin/server.py:104-124, 127-178].
147	
148	The frontend gets one additive fleet section — "Claude background sessions"
149	— rendered with the same card list, selection, and transcript hand-off
150	pattern `selectCell`/`selectDesignSession` already use
151	[admin/static/app.js:721-796], not a new page or visual language. Lifecycle
152	buttons (Stop, Respawn, Rm) use the same `window.confirm`-gated pattern as the
153	existing Interrupt control [admin/static/app.js:1284-1300], and Detach stays
154	a browser-only `EventSource.close()` with no process effect
155	[admin/static/app.js:803-811].
156	
157	### Rationale
158	
159	- **Subprocess, not a new client library or service.** `claude_adapter.py`
160	  already resolves the CLI binary and drives it via subprocess for headless
161	  runs [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:36-46, 291-299]; there is no HTTP API
162	  for background sessions to call instead — the CLI *is* the contract. This
163	  keeps the pattern consistent with the one Claude Code integration this
164	  repo already has, and avoids adding a daemon RPC client that isn't
165	  documented.
166	- **`claude logs` polling instead of `claude attach`.** `attach` is
167	  documented as an interactive terminal follow, the same category as
168	  `claude agents`'s own "requires an interactive terminal" caveat. Wiring a
169	  no-TTY subprocess to `attach` risks it blocking on terminal I/O or emitting
170	  control codes meant for a real terminal. `logs` is a plain stdout dump,
171	  safe to call on an interval and diff — the same shape as
172	  `scripts/supervise.py`'s existing poll-and-relay loop
173	  [scripts/supervise.py:81-94, 158-176, 243-269], just polling a CLI command
174	  instead of an HTTP session.
175	- **Reuse the `cell_id`-namespaced relay-into-`/api/events/<cell_id>` pattern.**
176	  `scripts/supervise.py` already proves this pattern for OpenCode: it invents
177	  a readable `cell_id` per native session (`_cell_id_for`,
178	  [scripts/supervise.py:151-155]) and relays that session's events into the
179	  Control Room's existing Redis event log/channel so the frontend needs no
180	  new stream type [scripts/supervise.py:158-176]. Background Claude sessions
181	  do the same under a `claude_bg_` prefix, so `admin/server.py`'s SSE
182	  endpoint, replay boundary, and frontend transcript renderer need no changes.
183	- **No steer/send-input control, anywhere in the surface.** The CLI reference
184	  has no equivalent to OpenCode's `delivery: queue|steer` prompt admission
185	  [admin/opencode_client.py:94-102]. Inventing one (e.g. by piping into a
186	  wrapped subprocess's stdin) would control a mechanism the CLI doesn't
187	  document as supported and could silently corrupt session state. The
188	  Control Room's job here is Observe (list, logs, daemon status) and a
189	  narrow, confirmed Control (start, stop/kill, respawn, rm, daemon stop) —
190	  not steering.
191	- **Reuse the existing model-alias table and workdir-allowlist pattern.**
192	  Background-session start should call `_resolve_claude_model`
193	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211] so a UI-selected model produces
194	  the exact same `--model` argument the headless adapter already produces,
195	  and should restrict `--cwd`/launch directory the same way design sessions
196	  restrict `workdir` to a configured allowlist
197	  [admin/server.py:81-101], rather than accepting an arbitrary path from the
198	  browser.
199	- **Daemon-stop is scoped as a rare, heavily-gated action, not a routine
200	  control.** `claude daemon stop` affects every session the supervisor hosts,
201	  not just ones the Control Room started. It is exposed only as an explicit,
202	  separately confirmed action, defaults to `--keep-workers` (sessions survive
203	  and the next supervisor reconnects to them) unless the operator
204	  affirmatively also wants to end running sessions, and is not offered from
205	  any bulk or default control.
206	
207	## 4. Constraints
208	
209	- Extend `admin/server.py` and `admin/static/` additively. Do not modify
210	  `admin/opencode_client.py`, `scripts/supervise.py`, or any
211	  `/api/design-sessions*` behavior — that surface belongs to a different
212	  feature owner and this feature must not change its endpoints, Redis keys,
213	  or semantics.
214	- Drive `claude` exclusively via `subprocess`, matching
215	  `src/instrument/claude_adapter.py`'s existing pattern. No new network
216	  service, no daemon RPC client, no polling of an undocumented socket
217	  protocol — only the CLI surfaces named in section 2.
218	- Do not implement, expose, or imply a send-input/steer control for a running
219	  background session. If the CLI reference gains one in the future, treat
220	  that as new investigation, not something to anticipate now.
221	- Reuse `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` and its retained-history/`replay_complete`
222	  contract [admin/server.py:450-490] for background-session transcripts. Do
223	  not add a second SSE endpoint shape or a new frontend stream type.
224	- Reuse the loopback + same-origin + JSON + `Idempotency-Key` mutation guard
225	  [admin/server.py:104-178] for every new `POST` endpoint (start, stop,
226	  respawn, rm, daemon stop), exactly as `/api/design-sessions/*` already does.
227	- Every destructive action — `stop`/`kill`, `rm`, `daemon stop` — is a
228	  one-way door from the operator's perspective and requires an explicit
229	  confirmation step in the UI before the request is sent, matching the
230	  existing Interrupt confirmation pattern [admin/static/app.js:1284-1300].
231	  `respawn` is control but not destructive (conversation survives) and does
232	  not require the same confirmation weight, though it should still be a
233	  deliberate click, not a default action.
234	- `claude daemon stop` defaults to `--keep-workers`; only an explicit,
235	  separately labeled operator choice omits it and allows sessions to be
236	  killed along with the supervisor.
237	- Restrict where background sessions can be started to a configured directory
238	  allowlist, reusing the shape of the existing `workdirs` mapping
239	  [admin/server.py:81-101]. Never accept an arbitrary filesystem path from
240	  the browser as a launch `--cwd`.
241	- Reuse `_resolve_claude_model`
242	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211] for model selection so background
243	  sessions and headless runs resolve framework model ids identically.
244	  `--advisor` is passed straight through as an optional string from a small
245	  fixed set (`fable`, `opus`, `sonnet`, or a full model id); do not build new
246	  advisor logic.
247	- No new build step, dependency, or frontend framework. Python + the existing
248	  vanilla JS/CSS static app remain the implementation surface, per the
249	  Control Room's existing constraints.
250	- Bound poll frequency, JSON body size, and log-tail size the same way
251	  `/api/design-sessions` already bounds request size and prompt length
252	  [admin/server.py:66-67]; an unavailable `claude` binary or daemon must
253	  degrade to a visible error state, not hang the Flask request thread.
254	
255	## 5. Acceptance Criteria
256	
257	1. [ ] `admin/claude_agents_client.py` wraps `claude agents --json --all`,
258	   `claude --bg`, `claude logs <id>`, `claude stop <id>`,
259	   `claude respawn <id>`, `claude rm <id>`, and `claude daemon status` /
260	   `claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]` as subprocess calls, each
261	   returning parsed JSON or raw text plus a distinguishable error for a
262	   missing binary, non-zero exit, or timeout.

1	# Challenge: Claude Code Background Sessions Scope
2	
3	Reviewed against `docs/scope.md`, the code it cites
4	(`admin/opencode_client.py`, `scripts/supervise.py`, `admin/server.py`,
5	`src/instrument/claude_adapter.py`, `admin/design_sessions.py`,
6	`admin/static/app.js`), and the live Claude Code CLI reference
7	(`https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference`), fetched directly for this
8	review rather than taken on faith.
9	
10	## 0. CLI facts: verified accurate
11	
12	Section 2's quoted commands and flags (`--bg`/`--background`, `claude
13	agents`/`--json`/`--all`/`--cwd`, `claude attach`, `claude logs`, `claude
14	daemon status`, `claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]`, `claude
15	stop`/`kill`, `claude respawn [--all]`, `claude rm`, `--advisor <model>`) were
16	re-fetched from the live reference for this review and match the scope
17	document essentially verbatim, including the "requires an interactive
18	terminal" caveat on `claude agents` and the "recent output" wording on
19	`claude logs`. The document's central claim — that the CLI is a documented,
20	scriptable contract for everything except send-input/steer — holds up. This
21	matters because the whole feature stands or falls on that contract being
22	right, and it is.
23	
24	## 1. Where I agree
25	
26	- **No invented steer/interrupt.** The CLI has no equivalent to OpenCode's
27	  `delivery: queue|steer` [admin/opencode_client.py:94-102], and the scope
28	  correctly refuses to fake one via subprocess stdin. This also matches the
29	  repo's own existing philosophy: `scripts/supervise.py`'s monitor is
30	  explicitly "flags only. A human decides the intervention"
31	  [scripts/supervise.py:9,48]. Not inventing a control the vendor doesn't
32	  document is the right call, not just a cautious one.
33	- **`claude logs` over `claude attach`/`claude agents` for headless
34	  polling.** Both of the latter are documented as needing a real TTY; `logs`
35	  is a plain stdout dump. Driving only the scriptable subset via subprocess
36	  is consistent with how `claude_adapter.py` already drives the CLI
37	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:291-299].
38	- **Reusing `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` under a `claude_bg_<id>` cell
39	  namespace** instead of a new SSE shape is the same trick
40	  `scripts/supervise.py` already uses for OpenCode (`_cell_id_for`,
41	  [scripts/supervise.py:151-155]) and it's the right one here too — zero new
42	  frontend stream types.
43	- **Daemon-stop defaulting to `--keep-workers`, gated separately from
44	  routine controls.** `daemon stop` is documented as affecting every session
45	  the supervisor hosts, not just Control-Room-started ones, and scoping it as
46	  a rare, explicitly-confirmed action with a safe default is proportionate to
47	  that blast radius.
48	- **Reusing `_resolve_claude_model` and the workdir-allowlist shape**
49	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211; admin/server.py:81-101] instead
50	  of building parallel model-resolution or path-validation logic is the
51	  correct anti-duplication call, and it's consistent with how
52	  `admin/design_sessions.py` already restricts `workdir_key` to an approved
53	  map [admin/design_sessions.py:284-288].
54	- **Reusing the loopback + JSON + Idempotency-Key mutation guard**
55	  [admin/server.py:104-124] for every new `POST` route rather than writing a
56	  second guard is correct; it's exactly what `/api/design-sessions/*` already
57	  does for every mutating endpoint.
58	
59	## 2. Where I disagree
60	
61	### 2.1 The roster is host-wide, not Control-Room-owned — this is a safety gap, not a detail
62	
63	`claude agents --json --all` lists **every** background session on the
64	machine, including ones an operator started by hand in a terminal, unrelated
65	to the Control Room. The scope's acceptance criteria (#2) only says the
66	roster comes from that call; nothing scopes it to sessions the Control Room
67	itself launched. That means the fleet UI will show Stop/Respawn/Rm buttons —
68	one-way-door actions per the scope's own constraint — on sessions the
69	operator didn't start and may not know about, with no visual distinction.
70	Contrast this with the daemon-stop action, where the scope *does* explicitly
71	call out "affects every session the supervisor hosts, not just ones started
72	from the Control Room" (§3 Rationale, criterion 9) — the same reasoning
73	should apply to the plain roster list, and it doesn't.
74	
75	**Alternative:** query `claude agents --cwd <path> --json --all` once per
76	configured workdir-allowlist entry (the CLI supports exactly this scoping
77	flag) instead of one unscoped `--all` call, and additionally track
78	Control-Room-launched session ids in a small Redis set written at `--bg`
79	start time. Render sessions found only via the `--cwd` scan but absent from
80	that set as "external — not started here," and require the strongest
81	confirmation copy (or disable Stop/Rm outright) for them. This costs one
82	Redis set and a few more `--cwd`-scoped calls; it does not touch the
83	`--all`-vs-scoped decision the daemon-stop rationale already implicitly
84	endorses.
85	
86	### 2.2 Relaying only the *selected* session loses history the OpenCode side never loses
87	
88	The decision routes log-diffing through "the currently selected/attached
89	session only" (§3 Decision). Compare `scripts/supervise.py`, which the scope
90	repeatedly cites as the pattern to mirror: `relay_once` maintains one relay
91	thread **per active session**, continuously, regardless of what's selected in
92	the UI [scripts/supervise.py:178-193]. That works for OpenCode because the
93	native server holds durable, gapless history independent of the Control
94	Room's polling — `iter_events` can always backfill full history on attach
95	[admin/opencode_client.py:114-137]. `claude logs <id>` has no such backing
96	store from the Control Room's point of view: the reference describes it as
97	"recent output," i.e. a bounded tail, not a durable full-history API. Combine
98	those two facts and a session that runs for a while before anyone selects its
99	card can have its early output permanently unrecoverable — there is no
100	retained window for a cell nobody was polling, and by the time it's selected
101	`claude logs` may no longer have the early lines to backfill from.
102	
103	**Alternative:** mirror `relay_once`'s actual behavior, not just its naming
104	convention — start a `claude logs`-diffing thread for every session returned
105	by the roster poll (bounded by the same `--cwd` scoping from 2.1), not just
106	the selected one, so retained history accumulates in Redis the same way it
107	does for OpenCode regardless of UI attention. If the resource cost of N
108	concurrent polling threads is the actual reason for the "selected only"
109	choice, say so explicitly and put a number on it (max concurrent relays,
110	poll interval) rather than leaving "selected only" implicit — either way,
111	acceptance criterion 4 should state plainly that Claude transcripts are
112	best-effort/tail-bounded, not the gapless equivalent OpenCode gets, so nobody
113	mistakes the "reuses the same SSE endpoint" plumbing for "reuses the same
114	fidelity guarantee."
115	
116	### 2.3 Embedding subprocess polling in the Flask dev server risks the resource the docstring already warns about
117	
118	`admin/server.py`'s own module docstring flags that `app.run(threaded=True)`
119	is "Flask's built-in single-process development server" and that every SSE
120	client "holds one request thread... for the life of the tab, so there is no
121	connection cap" [admin/server.py:16-20]. The scope's decision to add a
122	"module-level thread" that runs `claude agents --json --all` on an interval
123	plus (per 2.2, ideally N) `claude logs`-polling relay threads, each shelling
124	out via `subprocess`, adds more long-lived thread + blocking-subprocess
125	pressure to that same single process — on top of the SSE thread-per-tab load
126	the docstring already flags as needing a production gunicorn front-end for
127	multi-operator use. The scope explicitly rejects "a new always-on service"
128	(§3 Decision) without weighing this against the alternative the codebase
129	already has for exactly this shape of problem.
130	
131	**Alternative:** give the poller/relay the same separate-process treatment
132	`scripts/supervise.py` already has for OpenCode, e.g.
133	`scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py`: it owns all `subprocess` calls to
134	`claude`, writes the roster and relayed log lines straight to Redis, and
135	`admin/server.py` only ever reads Redis for `GET /api/claude-agents*` — the
136	same read-only relationship `api_matrix`/`api_events` already have to
137	`scripts/supervise.py`'s output. `POST` actions (start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon
138	stop) can stay synchronous subprocess calls inside Flask, since those are
139	short, bounded, one-shot commands, not long-lived polling loops — it's
140	specifically the *polling* that doesn't belong in the request-serving
141	process, not all subprocess use.
142	
143	### 2.4 The Problem framing promises more than the Approach delivers, silently
144	
145	The Problem section justifies this feature by pointing at "the Control
146	Room['s]... native supervisor surface for OpenCode," and names both halves
147	of it: `admin/opencode_client.py` (observe/control) *and*
148	`scripts/supervise.py`, described as flagging "stalled/off-track work for
149	human review" [docs/scope.md:5-8]. The Chosen Integration Approach then only
150	builds the `opencode_client.py`-equivalent half (list/observe/lifecycle
151	control) — there is no proposed equivalent to the flash-model monitor that
152	reads session activity and emits healthy/stalled/off_track flags. That may
153	well be the right phasing choice (get observe+control shipped first), but
154	the scope never says so — it cites the flagging behavior as motivation and
155	then quietly doesn't build it, which reads as an oversight rather than a
156	decision if a reader isn't cross-checking `scripts/supervise.py` themselves.
157	It's a real, buildable follow-on: `claude logs <id>` output is exactly the
158	kind of text `supervise_once`'s batching already knows how to summarize
159	[scripts/supervise.py:211-240], so nothing here is CLI-blocked.
160	
161	**Alternative:** either trim the Problem section's framing to the half
162	actually being built (observe + lifecycle control), or add one sentence to
163	§3/§4 stating that AI-flagging of background-session health is explicitly
164	out of scope for this phase and left as a follow-up once `claude logs`
165	polling exists to feed it. Either fixes the mismatch; leaving it unstated
166	does not.
167	
168	## 3. Recommendation
169	
170	Proceed to the spec phase with the CLI contract and the observe/control
171	shape as scoped — but resolve 2.1 (roster ownership scoping) and 2.4
172	(explicit phasing of the flagging gap) in the spec itself before writing
173	acceptance criteria, since both change what "done" means; 2.2 and 2.3 are
174	implementation-shape calls that can be settled during spec or left as
175	explicit, documented trade-offs if the team prefers the simpler
176	selected-only/embedded-poller path.

29	class OpenCodeError(RuntimeError):
30	    """Actionable failure returned by or encountered while calling OpenCode."""

32	    message: str

35	    def __str__(self) -> str:

39	class OpenCodeClient:
40	    """Call the native OpenCode v2 session and durable-event endpoints."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self, base_url: str, *, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:
43	        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
44	        self.timeout = timeout
45	
46	    def _json_request(
47	        self,
48	        method: str,
49	        path: str,
50	        body: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
51	        *,
52	        allow_empty: bool = False,
53	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
54	        """Issue one bounded JSON request and reject malformed success bodies."""
55	        payload = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
56	        headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
57	        if payload is not None:
58	            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
59	        request = Request(f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=payload, headers=headers, method=method)
60	        try:
61	            with urlopen(request, timeout=self.timeout) as response:  # noqa: S310 - configured loopback service
62	                raw = response.read(MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES + 1)
63	        except HTTPError as error:
64	            detail = error.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()

67	                error.code,

69	        except (URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as error:

72	        if len(raw) > MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES:

155	                        except json.JSONDecodeError:
156	                            event = {"type": "raw", "data": raw_data}

159	                        if event_id and not any(key in event for key in ("sequence", "aggregateSequence")):

163	                    data_size = 0

## 0. What this feature is, in one paragraph

The Control Room already surfaces OpenCode's native sessions through
`admin/opencode_client.py` (HTTP) and `scripts/supervise.py` (a separate
poll-and-relay process). Claude Code has no HTTP API for background
sessions — the `claude` CLI itself is the only documented contract
(`claude --bg`, `claude agents --json --all`, `claude logs`, `claude stop`/
`kill`, `claude respawn`, `claude rm`, `claude daemon status`/`stop`). This
feature adds a parallel fleet section, "Claude background sessions," that
lists those sessions, relays their output into the Control Room's existing
SSE transport, and offers a narrow, confirmed set of lifecycle controls —
without inventing any steering capability the CLI doesn't document.

## 1. Design overview

### 1.1 Scope of this phase

In scope: **observe** (roster, per-session transcript tail, daemon status)
and **lifecycle control** (start, stop/kill, respawn, rm, daemon stop) for
`claude --bg` sessions, reusing the Control Room's existing card/transcript
UI and SSE plumbing.

Out of scope, explicitly: an AI health-flagging monitor analogous to
`scripts/supervise.py`'s flash-model "healthy / stalled / off_track"
assessment loop over OpenCode sessions. `docs/scope.md`'s Problem section
motivates this feature by naming both halves of the OpenCode surface —
observe/control (`opencode_client.py`) *and* flagging (`supervise.py`) — but
the Chosen Integration Approach only builds the first half. §4.4 records this
as a deliberate phasing decision, not an oversight: `claude logs <id>`
output is exactly the kind of text `supervise_once`'s batching already knows
how to summarize, so a Claude-session flagging monitor is a real, buildable
follow-on once this phase's log relay exists to feed it — just not part of
this delivery.

### 1.2 Session ownership: the central design decision

Claude Code's `claude agents --json --all` lists **every** background
session the local `claude daemon` supervisor hosts, including ones an
operator started by hand in an unrelated terminal — the CLI has no concept
of "sessions this UI started." Left unaddressed, that means the Control
Room would render Stop/Respawn/Rm buttons on sessions it has no relationship
to. This spec resolves that (§4.1) by splitting every session the roster
returns into two classes:

- **Owned** — started via this feature's `POST /api/claude-agents`. Recorded
  in a Redis set (`claude_bg:owned_sessions`) at start time. Gets full
  lifecycle control, a continuously relayed transcript from launch, and the
  full card treatment.
- **External** — present in `claude agents --json --all` but not in the
  owned set. Gets a roster row with an "external — not started here" badge,
  a one-shot best-effort log fetch, and **no** lifecycle control affordance
  — Stop/Respawn/Rm are not rendered, and the corresponding endpoints reject
  the action server-side (not just client-side) if the id isn't owned.

This mirrors the reasoning `docs/scope.md` already applies to `claude daemon
stop` ("affects every session the supervisor hosts, not just ones started
from the Control Room") and extends it to the plain roster list, which the
original scope left unscoped.

### 1.3 Fleet layout

The existing fleet view (`admin/static/app.js`, cell cards + design-session
cards) gains one additive section, "Claude background sessions," rendered
with the same card list markup and selection pattern `selectCell`/
`selectDesignSession` already use [admin/static/app.js:721-801]. No new
page, panel type, or visual language.

Each card shows: session id (truncated with full id on hover/title attr),
status (`running`/`stopped`/`completed`/`unknown`, taken from the roster
JSON), task/title (truncated), model, cwd, started/updated timestamps, and
an **Owned**/**External** badge per §1.2. Owned cards render Stop, Respawn,
Rm, and Detach controls in a control panel below the transcript pane,
mirroring the existing Interrupt/Detach panel for design sessions
[admin/static/app.js:1267-1304] minus Interrupt (§3.4 explains why no
interrupt-equivalent exists) plus Respawn and Rm. External cards render only
Detach and a "fetch latest log tail" button.

A separate, always-visible **Daemon** panel (not per-card) shows `claude
daemon status` output read-only, plus a single, separately gated "Stop
daemon" control (§3.5).

### 1.4 Session id → renderable identity

A background session's CLI-native id becomes the Control Room's `cell_id`
for that session, namespaced as `claude_bg_<id>`, the same trick
`scripts/supervise.py`'s `_cell_id_for` already uses for OpenCode sessions
[scripts/supervise.py:151-155]. Concretely:

- The id is validated against a strict allowlist pattern
  (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`) everywhere it crosses a trust boundary — reading
  it from `claude agents --json` output, accepting it as a URL path segment,
  and using it to build a Redis key or `LivePublisher` cell id. An id that
  fails the pattern is dropped from the roster with a logged warning rather
  than passed through; this is the same discipline `_slugify` applies to
  OpenCode titles/models before building a `cell_id`
  [scripts/supervise.py:146-155], made stricter here because a background
  session id (unlike a free-text title) is expected to already be a stable
  machine identifier and any deviation is more likely an attack or a parsing
  bug than legitimate data.
- `GET /api/events/claude_bg_<id>` is the existing, unmodified
  `/api/events/<cell_id>` endpoint [admin/server.py:450-490] — no new SSE
  route, no new frontend `EventSource` handling. The frontend's
  `selectClaudeAgent(id, attach)` (new, mirroring `selectDesignSession`
  [admin/static/app.js:758-801]) just points `state.selectedId` at
  `claude_bg_<id>` and calls the existing `connectSelectedStream()`.
- The roster entry the browser renders and the `cell_id` used for its
  transcript are thus always derivable from each other by one string
  operation (`claude_bg_` + id / strip the prefix), so no separate id-mapping
  table is needed anywhere in the stack.

## 2. Observe path + endpoint contract

### 2.1 Why polling moves out of the Flask process

`admin/server.py`'s own docstring already flags that `app.run(threaded=True)`
is a single-process dev server where every SSE client holds one request
thread for the life of a tab [admin/server.py:16-20]. Adding a module-level
thread that shells out to `claude agents --json --all` on an interval, plus
one polling thread per relayed session, stacks more long-lived
thread-plus-blocking-subprocess load onto that same process. §4.3 adopts the
challenge's alternative: give Claude-agent polling the same treatment
`scripts/supervise.py` already gets for OpenCode — a separate process that
owns every polling `subprocess` call and writes only to Redis, with
`admin/server.py` staying a Redis reader for the roster/transcript paths.
Mutating actions (start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon status/stop) are short,
bounded, one-shot commands and stay as synchronous subprocess calls inside
Flask request handlers — it is specifically continuous polling, not all
subprocess use, that doesn't belong in the request-serving process.

### 2.2 `admin/claude_agents_client.py`

A subprocess wrapper mirroring the shape of `OpenCodeClient`
[admin/opencode_client.py] but calling the `claude` CLI instead of an HTTP
API, following the same binary-resolution and subprocess pattern
`claude_adapter.py` already uses for headless runs
[src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:36-46, 291-299]:

```
list_agents(cwd: str, *, all: bool = True, timeout: float = 15.0) -> list[dict]
    # claude agents --json [--all] --cwd <cwd>
start_agent(task: str, *, cwd: str, model: str, advisor: str | None,
            skip_permissions: bool, timeout: float = 15.0) -> dict
    # claude --bg "<task>" --cwd <cwd> [--model <model>] [--advisor <advisor>]
    #   [--dangerously-skip-permissions]
get_logs(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> str
    # claude logs <session_id>
stop_agent(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
    # claude stop <session_id>
respawn_agent(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
    # claude respawn <session_id>
rm_agent(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
    # claude rm <session_id>
daemon_status(*, timeout: float = 5.0) -> dict
    # claude daemon status  (exit code 1 => {"running": False})
daemon_stop(*, keep_workers: bool = True, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
    # claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]
```

Every call returns parsed JSON (or, for `get_logs`, raw text) on success and
raises a `ClaudeAgentsError` (mirroring `OpenCodeError`
[admin/opencode_client.py:28-36]) that distinguishes: binary not found,
non-zero exit (with captured stderr), malformed JSON, and timeout. No call
touches stdin — every subprocess is invoked with `stdin=DEVNULL` so a
misbehaving command can never block waiting for terminal input, which is the
concrete risk the scope already flags for `attach`/`agents` (§ "What is
explicitly NOT possible").

### 2.3 `scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py`

A new, separate long-running process, structurally parallel to
`scripts/supervise.py` but simpler (no monitor-session flagging loop — that's
explicitly deferred, §1.1):

- **Roster refresh.** Every `CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL` seconds (default
  10), for each path in the configured workdir allowlist (§3.2), runs
  `list_agents(path, all=True)`. Unions the results by id (a session can only
  be under one cwd, so this is a simple dict merge), tags each entry
  `owned: <id in claude_bg:owned_sessions>`, and writes the resulting JSON
  array to a Redis key `claude_bg:roster` with a TTL of `2 *
  CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL` seconds. The TTL means a dead/stalled
  supervisor produces a visibly stale (then absent) roster rather than a
  silently frozen one.
- **Transcript relay — owned sessions only.** For every roster entry with
  `owned: true` and a non-terminal status (or a terminal status reached less
  than `CLAUDE_AGENTS_RELAY_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 120, ago — so the final
  lines of a just-finished session are still captured), the supervisor
  ensures one relay thread is running, mirroring `_relay_session`
  [scripts/supervise.py:158-176]: loop, call `get_logs(id)`, diff against a
  per-session cursor (line count) stored in Redis
  (`claude_bg:cursor:<id>`), publish only the new lines through
  `LivePublisher(f"claude_bg_{id}")` [src/instrument/live.py:47-105], sleep,
  repeat. The thread exits once the grace period after a terminal status
  elapses, and `LivePublisher.set_status("done")` is called so the frontend's
  existing "stream ended" handling applies unchanged.
- **No relay for external sessions.** Sessions present in the roster but not
  in `claude_bg:owned_sessions` are never polled for logs by the supervisor.
  This is both the resource bound the challenge asked for (§4.3) and a
  courtesy/safety boundary: the Control Room does not continuously shell out
  against a process an operator started elsewhere without it being told to.
  §2.4 covers how an operator can still see an external session's recent
  output on demand.
- **Bounded concurrency.** Relay threads are capped at
  `CLAUDE_AGENTS_MAX_RELAYS` (default 20); if the owned-session count exceeds
  that, the supervisor logs a warning and relays the most-recently-updated
  sessions first. This is a real, documented cap, not a silent truncation —
  the roster itself (unaffected by the cap) still lists every owned session
  regardless of relay status, and a card without an active relay shows
  "transcript relay paused (fleet at capacity)" rather than an empty pane
  that looks like nothing happened.

### 2.4 New read endpoints in `admin/server.py`

- `GET /api/claude-agents` — reads `claude_bg:roster` from Redis. If the key
  is absent or the JSON fails to parse, returns `{"error":
  "supervisor_unavailable", "agents": []}` with a 200 (a rendering concern,
  not a hard failure — the fleet section shows a "supervisor not running"
  state, the rest of the Control Room is unaffected). Never calls
  `list_agents` synchronously — this is a pure Redis read, matching how
  `api_matrix` reads its own cached hashes [admin/server.py:384-421].
- `GET /api/claude-agents/<id>/logs` — for **external** sessions only (owned
  sessions get their transcript via `/api/events/claude_bg_<id>` and don't
  need this route); validates `id` against the same `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`
  pattern from §1.4, calls `claude_agents_client.get_logs(id)` synchronously
  with the client's bounded timeout, truncates the response to a fixed cap
  (e.g. 64 KB) matching the "bound... log-tail size" constraint, and returns
  it as plain text with a note that this is a one-shot, best-effort tail, not
  a live stream.
- `GET /api/claude-agents/daemon` — calls `daemon_status()` synchronously
  (bounded 5s timeout — a single fast status check, not a poll loop, so it
  stays inside Flask per §2.1's carve-out) and returns its JSON, or `{
  "running": false }` derived from exit code 1. Read-only; no control
  affordance is attached to this response, matching acceptance criterion 8.
- `GET /api/events/claude_bg_<id>` — no new code. This is the existing
  `/api/events/<cell_id>` route [admin/server.py:450-490], invoked with a
  `claude_bg_`-prefixed id. Retained-history replay, the `replay_complete`
  boundary, and heartbeat pings all behave exactly as they do for any other
  cell id, because the supervisor publishes through the same
  `LivePublisher`/Redis log+channel primitives every other relay uses
  [src/instrument/live.py:47-105].

### 2.5 Transcript fidelity — stated honestly

Owned-session transcripts are relayed continuously from shortly after launch
(§2.3), so in practice they are close to gapless — the same shape of
guarantee OpenCode sessions get from `scripts/supervise.py`'s
`relay_once`/`_relay_session` [scripts/supervise.py:178-193]. But the
underlying primitive is different in kind, not just in polling cadence:
`claude logs <id>` is documented as printing "recent output," a bounded
tail with no stated retention window, not a durable, gapless history API the
way OpenCode's `/api/session/{id}/event` SSE stream is
[admin/opencode_client.py:114-137]. Two consequences follow, and both are
stated in the UI and in acceptance criterion 4 rather than left implicit:

1. There is a small window — bounded by `CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL`,
   default 10s — between `claude --bg` returning a session id and the
   supervisor's first relay poll picking it up. Output produced in that
   window is not lost *if* `claude logs` still has it in its tail on the
   first poll (very likely at 10s for a session that just started), but this
   spec makes no stronger guarantee than that.
2. If `claude logs`'s own retention window is ever shorter than expected
   (e.g. under sustained high-volume output), lines could be dropped between
   two consecutive polls with no way for the Control Room to detect the gap,
   because `claude logs` exposes no cursor/offset primitive to detect
   under-run against — only content to diff against last-seen text. This is
   a limitation of the CLI contract, not an implementation gap; if a future
   CLI version adds an offset- or cursor-based tail command, this design
   should switch to it.

External-session transcripts (§2.4's one-shot `/logs` fetch) carry the same
"recent output, not full history" caveat, more visibly so, since there is no
continuous relay building a longer retained window at all.

## 3. Control path + door discipline

### 3.1 Mutation guard

Every new `POST` route reuses the loopback + same-origin + JSON +
`Idempotency-Key` guard `admin/server.py` already enforces for
`/api/design-sessions/*`
[admin/server.py:104-124, 127-178] — implemented as a small sibling helper,
`_claude_agent_mutation_body()`, with the same checks (loopback remote addr,
loopback `Host`, matching `Origin`, `application/json`, size cap, required
`Idempotency-Key`) rather than a parameterized shared function, to honor the
constraint that `/api/design-sessions*` behavior must not change
[docs/scope.md §4]. The existing `_idempotent_design_response` reservation
pattern (Redis `SET NX` + replay-on-retry) is reused the same way, under a
`claude-agent:<operation>:<id>` cache-key namespace so a retried Stop
request can't double-fire.

### 3.2 `POST /api/claude-agents` — start

Body: `{"workdir": "<allowlist key>", "task": "<string>", "model":
"<optional string>", "advisor": "<optional enum>"}`.

- `workdir` must be a key in a configured allowlist, `FINOPS_CLAUDE_AGENT_WORKDIRS`
  (same `PATH{os.pathsep}PATH...` env shape as
  `FINOPS_DESIGN_WORKDIRS` [admin/server.py:85-94], parsed by a small
  sibling function rather than by extending `_design_sessions()`, again to
  avoid touching the design-session code path). A raw filesystem path from
  the browser is never accepted, matching the same rule
  `DesignSessionManager` already applies to `workdir_key`
  [admin/design_sessions.py:284-288].
- `task` is bounded the same way `intent`/`prompt` are for design sessions
  (`MAX_DESIGN_PROMPT_CHARS`-equivalent cap).
- `model`, if present, is passed through `_resolve_claude_model`
  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211] so a UI-selected model produces
  the identical `--model` argument the headless adapter would produce for
  the same id.
- `advisor`, if present, must be one of a fixed set (`fable`, `opus`,
  `sonnet`) or match a full model-id shape; it is passed straight through as
  `--advisor <value>` with no other logic, per the scope's constraint.
- The launch always includes `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, consistent
  with every other Claude CLI invocation this framework already makes
  headlessly [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:291-299] — Control-Room-
  launched sessions are unattended by construction, the same as headless
  runs. Per the CLI reference, this flag persists across a `respawn` for the
  life of the session.
- On success, the client's `start_agent` result includes the new session id
  (parsed from `claude --bg`'s stdout, which the reference states prints the
  session id and management commands). The handler adds that id to
  `claude_bg:owned_sessions` (Redis `SADD`, no TTL — ownership is permanent
  for the id's lifetime; the set is only pruned when `rm` succeeds, §3.4)
  before returning `{"ok": true, "id": "<id>"}` to the browser. The next
  supervisor poll tick (≤ `CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL` seconds later) picks
  the session up as owned and starts its relay, per §2.3.

### 3.3 `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/stop` and `/respawn`

Both require the id to be present in `claude_bg:owned_sessions`; if not,
the handler returns `403 {"error": "session not started from the Control
Room; manage it with the claude CLI directly"}` **before** shelling out —
this is the server-side half of the ownership boundary from §1.2, not just a
hidden button.

- **Stop** (`claude stop <id>`, `kill` is the CLI's alias for the same
  operation, so this feature exposes only `stop`) is a one-way door in the
  sense the scope's constraint means: it ends the running process
  immediately, and the UI must not let that happen from a stray click. The
  frontend requires `window.confirm` before sending the request, matching
  the existing Interrupt-confirmation pattern
  [admin/static/app.js:1284]. The response states plainly that the
  conversation is preserved and can be resumed with **Respawn** — stop is
  not "conversation deleted," it is "process ended, resumable."
- **Respawn** (`claude respawn <id>`) restarts a running-or-stopped session
  with its conversation intact. It is control, not destructive — the scope
  explicitly says it "does not require the same confirmation weight, though
  it should still be a deliberate click, not a default action." The UI
  implements this as a plain button (no `window.confirm`), not bound to any
  keyboard shortcut or auto-triggered flow, and the response/roster entry is
  checked to confirm the conversation id is unchanged before the card
  re-renders as running.

### 3.4 `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/rm`

Requires ownership (§3.3's same check) and `window.confirm` (rm removes the
session from `claude agents`'s own list; while the reference states the
transcript stays on disk and remains reachable via `claude --resume`, that
resume path is outside this UI, so from the Control Room's perspective this
is effectively a one-way door on the *card*, even though the data isn't
deleted). On success, the handler also removes the id from
`claude_bg:owned_sessions` and its relay cursor key, and the response text
states explicitly: "removed from the Claude agents list; transcript remains
on disk and is reachable via `claude --resume <id>` outside the Control
Room."

### 3.5 `POST /api/claude-agents/daemon/stop`

The most severe control this feature exposes, because `claude daemon stop`
affects **every** session the local `claude daemon` hosts, including
external ones this UI has no relationship to and cannot even fully
enumerate confidently (an external session could be under a cwd outside the
configured allowlist and never appear in this feature's roster at all, yet
still be killed by this call). Accordingly:

- Body: `{"keep_workers": true}` by default; the operator must pass
  `{"keep_workers": false}` explicitly to also end every running session
  along with the supervisor. The handler rejects a missing `keep_workers`
  field rather than defaulting silently in the request-parsing layer, so the
  choice is always explicit in the logged request body, not just the UI
  copy.
- The frontend requires a `window.confirm` whose copy names the blast
  radius plainly, e.g.: *"Stop the Claude agents daemon? This affects every
  background session on this machine, not just ones started from the
  Control Room."* — and a second, visually distinct confirm/toggle before
  `keep_workers: false` can even be sent, so "end every session" cannot be
  reached by the same single click that stops the supervisor.
- This control lives in the daemon panel (§1.3), never inside a per-session
  card and never as part of any bulk/multi-select action.

### 3.6 Door-discipline summary

| Action | Reversible? | Confirmation | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start | n/a (creates) | none (deliberate form submit) | one session, owned workdir only |
| Stop/kill | Process ends now; conversation resumable via Respawn | `window.confirm` | one owned session |
| Respawn | Fully reversible (that's its purpose) | deliberate click, no confirm dialog | one owned session |
| Rm | Removed from list; transcript stays on disk, resumable only outside this UI | `window.confirm` | one owned session |
| Daemon stop (keep-workers) | Supervisor restarts and reconnects; sessions survive | `window.confirm`, blast-radius copy | every session on the host |
| Daemon stop (end sessions) | Every hosted session ends | `window.confirm` + separate explicit toggle | every session on the host |
| Detach | N/A — browser only | none needed | browser tab only, no process effect |

## 4. Challenge adjudication

Every point in `docs/challenge.md` is addressed below. §0 and §1 of the
challenge (CLI-fact verification and five points of agreement) are adopted
without modification and are folded into §1–§3 above without a separate
row, since there was nothing to resolve. The four disagreement points
(§2.1–§2.4) get individual verdicts.

| # | Challenge point | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | **2.1** Unscoped `--all` roster mixes external sessions in with no visual distinction, exposing Stop/Rm on sessions the operator didn't start | **Adopted, with a stronger mechanism than proposed.** Challenge suggested `--cwd`-scoped polling + an owned-set + "strongest confirmation copy (or disable outright)" for external sessions. This spec adopts `--cwd`-scoped polling and the owned-set (§1.2, §2.3), and picks the "disable outright" branch rather than stronger confirmation copy: external sessions get no Stop/Respawn/Rm affordance in the UI *and* the corresponding endpoints reject the action server-side if the id isn't owned (§3.3). Outright disabling is simpler to reason about and audit than a confirmation-copy variant that still has a code path to the destructive action; there's no legitimate Control-Room workflow that needs to stop a session it didn't start. |
| 4.2 | **2.2** Relaying only the selected session loses early history a session accumulates before anyone selects its card, unlike OpenCode's gapless relay | **Synthesized.** Full adoption of "relay every roster session continuously" was rejected because, combined with 4.1's ownership split, it would mean continuously polling external sessions the Control Room has no business polling. Instead: owned sessions (the only ones this feature can act on anyway) get continuous relay starting within one poll interval of launch (§2.3), which is close to OpenCode's guarantee for the sessions that matter to this UI; external sessions get on-demand one-shot log fetches only (§2.4), never continuous relay. §2.5 states explicitly, in both this document and acceptance criterion 4, that `claude logs` is a bounded-tail primitive, not the gapless equivalent OpenCode's SSE history gives — exactly the honesty check the challenge asked for, without over-building continuous relay for sessions this UI shouldn't be polling in the first place. |
| 4.3 | **2.3** Embedding polling threads + subprocess calls in the single-process Flask dev server risks the exact resource pressure its own docstring warns about | **Adopted.** `scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py` (§2.1, §2.3) takes over all polling and relay subprocess calls, structurally parallel to `scripts/supervise.py`. `admin/server.py` only reads Redis for `GET /api/claude-agents` and the transcript route. Short, bounded, one-shot mutating commands (start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon status/daemon stop) stay as synchronous Flask-side subprocess calls, per the challenge's own carve-out — it is the *polling* that doesn't belong in the request-serving process, not all subprocess use. |
| 4.4 | **2.4** The Problem section motivates this feature by naming both the observe/control half and the AI-flagging half of `scripts/supervise.py`, but only the first is built, unstated | **Adopted.** §1.1 states explicitly that AI health-flagging for Claude background sessions is out of scope for this phase and is a real, buildable follow-on once this phase's `claude logs` relay exists to feed it (the challenge's own observation that `supervise_once`'s batching already knows how to summarize this shape of text). This is the "add one sentence to §3/§4" resolution the challenge offered as sufficient, applied here instead as an explicit phase-scope statement. |

## 5. Acceptance criteria

1. `admin/claude_agents_client.py` wraps `claude agents --json --all --cwd
   <path>`, `claude --bg`, `claude logs <id>`, `claude stop <id>`, `claude
   respawn <id>`, `claude rm <id>`, `claude daemon status`, and `claude
   daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]` as subprocess calls (stdin closed on
   every call), each returning parsed JSON/text or a distinguishable error
   for a missing binary, non-zero exit, malformed JSON, or timeout.
2. `scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py` runs as a separate process; it is
   the only thing that polls `claude agents --json --all` or `claude logs`.
   It writes `claude_bg:roster` (TTL'd, tagged `owned`) and relays log lines
   for owned, non-terminal-or-recently-terminal sessions only, into
   `LivePublisher(f"claude_bg_{id}")`, capped at `CLAUDE_AGENTS_MAX_RELAYS`
   concurrent relay threads with the overflow surfaced in the UI, not
   silently dropped.
